description: Source of truth for the sf new command surface used by the tool-saasfoundry skill. Each entry maps an intent JSON field to its corresponding --flag on `sf new`. Both plan-new.sh and the skill's discovery conversation read this file — keep them in sync by editing here, never by hardcoding flag names elsewhere.

structure.description: Monorepo (single repo) vs multirepo (backend + frontend split)

advancedSkills.description: Comma-separated list of advanced skills to install

agents.description: Comma-separated coding-tool profiles to declare in the generated harness. Omission preserves the legacy implicit Claude Code declaration.

srsEnable.description: Opt-in SRS bootstrap. When true, requires srsBackend, srsParentPageInput, and a Notion token.

srsBackend.description: Backend hosting the SRS workspace. V1 supports Notion only.

srsParentPageInput.description: URL or ID of the Notion parent page that will host the SRS root page. Must be shared with the Notion integration.

srsIngestEnable.description: Opt-in to ingest existing notes / specs into the SRS after bootstrap. Stamps `tools.srs.pendingIngestion` in the manifest ; the sf-srs skill runs the ingestion conversation next time you open the project in Claude Code.

srsIngestParentInput.description: URL or ID of the Notion parent page that contains the existing notes to ingest. Must be shared with the Notion integration.

workflow.description: Workflow preset name, or 'none' / --no-workflow to skip

profile.description: What to install: full (stack + AI harness), harness (AI layer onto an existing project), stack (technical base only)

pwa.description: Make the generated app installable as a desktop application (web manifest + service worker)

structure.monorepo: Default for solo devs, small teams, and projects where backend+frontend ship together. Single repo simplifies CI, versioning, and PR scope.
structure.multirepo: Choose when backend and frontend are owned by different teams, deploy on independent schedules, or need per-side access controls.

emailService.mailersend: Recommend when the project needs transactional email (password reset, invites, receipts). The module ships ready-to-use templates.
emailService.none: Default for prototypes, internal tools, or when email is already handled upstream.

s3Setup.docker: Default for local development — spins up MinIO via docker-compose.
s3Setup.credentials: Choose for staging/prod against AWS S3 or an S3-compatible provider (R2, Backblaze, DigitalOcean Spaces).
s3Setup.manual: Choose when infra is provisioned outside SaaSFoundryAI and credentials come from an external secret manager.

analytics.true: Recommend when tracking user activity or business metrics matters early. Installs a privacy-respecting analytics module.
analytics.false: Default for MVPs — adding analytics later via `sf update --add-modules analytics` is a one-liner.

srsEnable.true: Recommend when product requirements should be centralised for AI agents. Creates a Notion root page where Epics are hosted as direct children, under a parent page shared with the integration.
srsEnable.false: Default — opt-in later via `sf update --add-modules srs --srs-backend notion --srs-parent-page-input <urlOrId>`.

srsIngestEnable.true: Recommend when the user already has legacy notes / specs in Notion they want imported as Epics / FRs. The CLI only records the intent ; the sf-srs skill drives the actual ingestion conversationally on next Claude Code open.
srsIngestEnable.false: Default — the user can always ingest notes later by setting `tools.srs.pendingIngestion` manually or re-running `sf new`.

profile.full: Default. The user is starting from nothing, or from a throwaway POC they do not intend to keep. Scaffolds the technical stack AND the AI harness.
profile.harness: The user already has a codebase they are keeping. Deposits the AI layer (workflow, skills, SRS) onto the existing repository — no stack is scaffolded, no project directory is created. Ask before assuming: a POC the user wants to rewrite is a `full` case, a POC they want to build on is a `harness` case.
profile.stack: The user wants the technical base without the AI collaboration layer. Rare — confirm it is deliberate rather than a misunderstanding of what the harness does.

pwa.true: Default. Costs nothing to a user who ignores it — a manifest and a service worker, invisible unless installed. No credentials, no external service.
pwa.false: Recommend only when the product should deliberately not be installable, or when the author wants to own the service-worker strategy themselves.
